overview.description: Papillon (Butterfly) is a classic French fishing-type card game, conceptually similar to Scopa but with its own distinct bonus system and 'Talon' (stock) mechanics. Players use cards from their hand to capture cards from the table, either by matching ranks or sums. It is beloved for its evocative bonus names ('Grasshopper', 'Little Beetle') and its emphasis on being the first to 'fly away' by emptying one's hand. It is primarily a game of observation and tactical capturing.

history.origins: Dates back to the 18th century as a social salon game in France. It shares DNA with Italian fishing games like Scopa and the Middle Eastern game of Basra.
timeline: 1760s: Earliest mentions in French 'Academie des Jeux'.
1850s: Rules for 'The Grasshopper' sweep are formalized.
1920s: Remains popular in regional French cafes before being modernised.
Present: A niche historical game often played at heritage festivals.
history.evolution: The scoring shifted from purely trick-based to a weighted 'Jeton' (token) system to allow for gambling-style play.
history.cultural: The name 'Papillon' refers to the way a player 'flutters' through their hand to reveal a winning trick.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Each player receives 3 cards initially; 7 more face-up to the tableau (3 players) or 4 (4 players); remainder as talon. After each round when hands are empty, deal 3 more each from talon.
setup.dealing: Deal 3 cards each to hand (first hand to dealer's left), then 7 face-up to the tableau (4 in four-hand). Stack the remainder face down as talon. When all hands are empty, deal 3 more each from talon.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing cards and clearing the table; be the first to empty your hand after the talon is exhausted (papillon) to sweep the pool.
rules.gameplay: Players in turn play one card to capture: a table card of the same rank, or a set of table cards whose total equals the played card, or three of a rank from hand to capture the fourth from the table. Captured cards form a trick placed face down. If unable to capture (e.g. after a sauterelle sweep), the player trails all hand cards face up to the tableau. When all hands are empty, the dealer gives 3 more cards each from the talon. When the talon is exhausted, the first to empty their hand by taking a trick wins the deal (papillon) and sweeps the pool.
keyRules: Capture by same rank, by sum (played card equals total of table cards), or three-of-a-rank to take the fourth from table.
If you cannot capture, you must trail (play all hand cards face up to the tableau).
Sauterelle: sweeping all table cards forces the next player to trail.
Winner of the deal is first to empty hand by taking a trick after talon is exhausted; tie-break: dealer, second hand, first hand.

strategy.basic: Keep track of the numbers. If you have an 8, and there's a 5 and a 3 on the table, take them immediately to score more cards. Don't trail high cards (Aces/Kings) unless you have no other choice, as they are likely to be captured by opponents in the next turn.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Sauterelle' Denial: If you see the table is down to just a few cards that could be easily summed up (like a 2, 4, 1), and it's almost your opponent's turn, try to capture just ONE of those cards, even if it's less efficient. This 'breaks the chain' and prevents them from getting the Grasshopper bonus.
strategy.advanced: Stamina Management: In Papillon, being the first to empty your hand confers a bonus. If you have cards that can capture combinations, use them late. Early in the hand, focus on single-card matches (like Jack for Jack) to keep your combination-options open for when the table becomes more crowded.
tips: Aces are worth more in specific variationsâ€”check the local rules for 'Ace Pay' bonuses.
Remember: If you capture three 9s while holding the fourth, you get the 'Beetle' bonus. If those 9s are on the table, wait for the right moment!

list.name: Four-hand Papillon
list.description: Four players; dealer lays only 4 upcards on the tableau instead of 7. Otherwise the same as three-player.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Tableau size differs by player count; engine constants for this variant not yet mapped.

list.name: Modern rules
list.description: Simplified scoring: each player antes 1 or 2 jetons to the pot; each card trailed (except Aces) pays 1 jeton to the pot; each Ace trailed is paid 1 jeton by each opponent to the player; Papillon wins and sweeps the pot, or most cards wins if no-one achieves Papillon.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Scoring and ante rules differ; engine overrides for this variant not yet mapped.

difficulty.easy: Fails to see sum-based captures; always trails high cards; ignores bonuses.
difficulty.medium: Reasonable sum-calculation; targets the Grasshopper bonus; manages hand size well.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Bonus Sniping'; perfectly calculates the risk of trailing vs. capturing; master of the 'Sauterelle' denial strategy.

phases.label: Play
phases.notes: First hand (right of dealer) plays first; play continues counterclockwise. Capture or trail until talon exhausted and a player empties hand by taking a trick.

edgeCases.text: Sauterelle (grasshopper): a player who sweeps all table cards forces the next player to trail; that player must play all hand cards face up to the tableau.
Hanneton (beetle): capturing three table cards of the same rank while holding the fourth in hand earns a bonus.
Petit Papillon: emptying the hand by taking a trick while the talon still has cards; that player drops out until the next deal from the talon.
If more than one player empties hand in succession after talon is exhausted, winner is determined by order: dealer, second hand, first hand.
If no player can empty their hand at end of deal, the last to trail receives a consolation; remaining table cards go to the last player who took a trick.

engine.deckDescription: A standard 52-card French deck with four suits and thirteen ranks; no jokers. Papillon (French fishing) is played with six to nine cards per player depending on count; players capture cards from the table by matching rank or building sets.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) each contain thirteen cards. In this fishing game, cards are captured by playing a card that matches the rank of a table card or that forms a sum with it.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through 2 in each suit. Capture is by matching rank or by playing a card that adds with a table card to a specified total; clearing the table and scoring points are the goals of the game.
engine.dealPattern: 3 cards each to hand, 7 face-up to tableau (3 players) or 4 (4 players), remainder as talon; after each round of play when hands are empty, deal 3 more each from talon.
